commit_message:
[Codegen][CPU] Add x86 AVX-512 VNNI vpdpbusd MMA intrinsic.

Adds `vpdpbusd` — the AVX-512-VNNI byte dot-product — as a data-tiled
MMA intrinsic. It is the first asymmetric MMA: the first byte source
is unsigned, the second is signed, so the natural and swapped
orientations need different arg-routing at the call site (unlike the
LHS/RHS-symmetric FMA / dpbf16ps / vpdpwssd / pmaddw already
supported).

Two new enum values, `MMA_X86_AVX512VNNI_1x16x4_I32_UI8_I8` and its
M↔N-swapped sibling `MMA_X86_AVX512VNNI_16x1x4_I32_I8_UI8`, both
lower to `llvm.x86.avx512.vpdpbusd.512`. The swapped lowering flips
its (lhs, rhs) call args so the unsigned operand still lands in the
first slot.

Signedness handling — per IREE convention, vector tile types in IR are
signless, with the signed/unsigned distinction carried on the
encoding's `element_types`. `getABCElementTypes(intrinsic)` now
returns `ui8` where applicable, used by the cost model and validator
for matching against an encoding's `element_types`;
`getUndistributedTileTypes` strips the signedness when constructing
tile types. The validator and cost-model `getIntrinsicInfo` bypass
`getUndistributedTileTypes` and read shape + types straight from the
intrinsic via `getRowMajorTilesMNKShape` and `getABCElementTypes`,
which become public for that reason.

The prerequisite "distinct LHS/RHS types" PR added the
`e2e_matmul_cpu_dt_inner_tiled_ui8_i8_i32` test on the `generic`
variant only; this commit adds the `avx512vnni` variant that
actually selects the new intrinsic.

Progress towards #24323.

commit_message:
Preserve argmax combiner attrs when splitting reductions

Record the matched argmax combiner attributes and replay them when split reduction regenerates the canonical or StableHLO/JAX select-style combiner.

This keeps frontend-provided attributes such as arith fast-math flags on the regenerated floating-point ops in both partial and final reductions.

Signed-off-by: Yuwei Sun <yuweis2@illinois.edu>

commit_message:
Fix MapLoad for dynamic shapes (#24476)

`combine-source-layout-transformation` was building each new
`map_load`'s `tensor.empty` destination with
`tensor::getMixedSizes(consumer.getResult())`.
For a dynamically-shaped consumer (e.g. `extract_slice → expand_shape →
extract_slice → pad`), once the consumer was replaced by the new
`map_load`, the materialized `tensor.dim %consumer_result, i` queries
silently became `tensor.dim %new_map_load, i` and fed the very
`tensor.empty` driving that `map_load`'s destination : yielding both an
SSA dominance violation and a self-referential cycle
(`tensor.empty(tensor.dim(%new_ml, 0))` with `%new_ml
= map_load ... into %that_empty`).

This PR fixes the above by routing all such size queries through
reifyShapeOfResult, so dynamic dims are expressed in terms of the
consumer op's *operands* and never the result that's about to be
replaced.

Fixes #24461.

Signed-off-by: Abhishek Varma <abhvarma@amd.com>

commit_message:
[LinalgExt] Classify im2col convolution batch dims as m_pos dims (#24478)

Redefines the classification of convolution dimensions in the im2col op
when converting convolution to GEMM + im2col, and fixes a semantic
inconsistency with the treatment of convolution batch dims in the im2col
op. Batch dims in the convolution only appear in the image operand, so
they actually become M dims in the resulting GEMM, but the old
classification would place them in the batch_pos list.

This PR fixes the semantic error and puts convolution batch dims into
m_pos instead. In order to preserve the consistent handling of m_pos
dims in the im2col lowerings and verification, the batch dims are given
synthetic filter window metadata (unit strides, dilations, and window
size), which simplifies the im2col op lowering and verification
implementation. There is no reason the im2col op needs to know that the
dim came from a convolution batch dim, since im2col only needs a well
defined access pattern, for which this synthetic metadata is sufficient.

Benchmarks were tested locally on MI350, and there is no impact on
performance. This is expected, since layouts and the results of codegen
do not change, and this is only a change to the im2col metadata.

Assisted by: Codex

Signed-off-by: Max Dawkins <max.dawkins@gmail.com>

down the ops and fuse them into bindings, if possible. If it is not
possible, they become MapStoreOp so the sequence of the ops all
implement tiling interface.

Both solutions are required, and the revision adds the former
optimization to the pass.

The additional change is avoiding tile size adjustment from pack op when
the root op is an attention op. It'd break the fusion, because it is not
a perfect tiling case. It is intended to leave the pack op outside the
fusion, as attention is a big op and we respect its tiling config.

Fixes https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/23920

[Codegen][GPU] Relax 32-bit reduction/arg_compare ceiling for VectorDistribute (#24432)

The upstream PR

commit_message:
[AMDGPU] PM4 Command Buffer (#24452)


This adds an experimental PM4 command-buffer execution path to the
AMDGPU HAL. The default path remains AQL. PM4 is selected only when
explicitly requested with `--amdgpu_command_buffer_mode=pm4`, or when
`--amdgpu_command_buffer_mode=auto` sees a reusable dispatch-only
command buffer on a GPU ISA with validated PM4 dispatch-command-buffer
capabilities.

The central idea is to keep AQL as the queue and synchronization
envelope while changing the reusable command-buffer payload. The
existing AQL command-buffer path still replays one AQL dispatch packet
per recorded dispatch. That is a good general substrate, but it makes
dense reusable command buffers packet-count bound. The PM4 path records
dispatch-only reusable command buffers into a resident PM4 indirect
buffer, then submits that resident IB through an AQL PM4-IB vendor
packet. Static command buffers point directly at resident kernarg
templates. Dynamic command buffers upload only the invocation binding
table and run a small GPU fixup dispatch before launching the PM4 IB.

In other words, queue ordering, semaphore waits, completion, and host
queue integration stay on the existing AQL path. The dense
command-buffer body moves from "N AQL dispatch packets" to "one resident
PM4 IB", or "one fixup dispatch plus one resident PM4 IB" for dynamic
bindings.

### What changed

- Adds PM4 dispatch packet helpers, barrier helpers, kernel descriptor
decoding, and unit/live tests for the packet families used by this path.
- Adds an AMDGPU PM4 command-buffer implementation for dispatch-only
reusable command buffers.
- Adds resident PM4 storage management, host-copy and async-copy
publication modes, dynamic binding-table fixup records, and queue
execution through AQL PM4-IB packets.
- Adds PM4 command-buffer profiling support for queue/dispatch timing
where the selected GPU timestamp packet strategy can produce timestamp
ranges.
- Adds a benchmark target for PM4 command-buffer recording,
finalization, and replay accounting.
- Tightens capability selection so validated PM4 dispatch-command-buffer
support is enabled only for the GPU ISAs we have actually tested so far:
`gfx1100` and `gfx942`.
- Leaves a deliberate hardware bring-up escape hatch:
`--amdgpu_experimental_pm4_command_buffers` enables the unvalidated
gfx9-gfx12 PM4 dispatch-command-buffer packet set for future ASIC
experiments. Without that flag, unvalidated gfx families stay on the
base AQL path even if they are known to support AQL PM4-IB for profiling
or other narrower uses.

### Performance

The strongest measured case is a dense reusable command buffer: 10,000
alternating dispatches from two kernels, 20 percent local overlap, and a
100-entry binding table. These are replay measurements: recording and
finalization have already happened, and the timed region submits the
command buffer and waits for completion.

On the local `gfx1100` RDNA3 machine:

| Path | 10K replay time | Per dispatch | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| AQL dynamic bindings | 41.43 ms | 4.14 us | 1.0x |
| PM4 GPU fixup | 5.93 ms | 0.59 us | 7.0x |
| AQL static arguments | 41.12 ms | 4.11 us | 1.0x |
| PM4 static arguments | 5.13 ms | 0.51 us | 8.0x |

The static comparison is the cleanest mechanism proof. AQL static has
already removed per-invocation kernarg writes, but it still drains
10,000 AQL dispatch packets. PM4 static drains one resident PM4 command
stream. The dynamic PM4 row pays the expected fixup cost, but
per-invocation host traffic is proportional to the binding table: 800
bytes for 100 pointers, not per-dispatch kernarg traffic and not a
rebuilt command stream.

On the NOD `gfx942` MI300X probe, the same 10K alternating-dispatch
shape showed the same command-representation effect in the lower-level
AQL PM4-IB harness:

| Path | 10K GPU drain | Per dispatch | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| AQL, prepublished kernargs | 19.54 ms | 1.95 us | 1.0x |
| AQL, kernargs per run | 19.91 ms | 1.99 us | 1.0x |
| AQL PM4-IB static | 4.15 ms | 0.415 us | 4.7x to 4.8x |
| AQL PM4-IB dynamic fixup | 4.19 ms | 0.419 us | about 4.7x |

The RDNA3 and CDNA numbers should not be compared against each other as
architecture claims. They were taken on different machines, with
different harnesses, and with different levels of benchmark hygiene. The
important common result is structural: PM4 removes the per-dispatch AQL
packet from dense reusable command-buffer replay.

### Why this is the right shape

AQL remains the right HAL queue substrate. It already provides the
ROCR/HSA integration we need for queue submission, semaphore waits,
completion signaling, and the existing host queue ordering model.
Replacing that whole substrate would add risk without addressing the
main replay bottleneck.

The bottleneck is inside the reusable command-buffer payload. AQL
command buffers can prepublish static arguments and reduce host work,
but they cannot make a 10,000-dispatch command buffer stop being 10,000
AQL dispatch packets.
PM4 gives us the missing representation: resident command blocks that
the CP can walk directly, with compact dynamic state patched on device
when bindings change.

That is also the better long-term direction for command-buffer
evolution: resident IBs compose naturally with IB chaining, device-side
command-buffer scheduling, dynamic binding-table patching, and future
control-flow-like model execution. AQL still frames the outer execution;
PM4 gives dense replay a payload granularity that matches what we need.

### Rollout and caveats

- Default behavior is unchanged: `--amdgpu_command_buffer_mode=aql`.
- `auto` only selects PM4 for reusable dispatch-only command buffers
when the physical device advertises the validated PM4
dispatch-command-buffer capability set. Transfer command buffers,
one-shot command buffers, inline execution, and unsupported profiling
modes fall back to AQL.
- Validated automatic PM4 dispatch-command-buffer support is currently
limited to `gfx1100` and `gfx942`. Other gfx9-gfx12 targets require the
explicit `--amdgpu_experimental_pm4_command_buffers` hardware bring-up
flag.
- The supported-platform caveat is real: we have exercised a small
number of systems so far, not a broad ASIC/driver/firmware matrix. PM4
packet encodings, acquire/cache behavior, kernarg preload details, and
timestamp packet strategies need to stay capability-gated until each
target has hardware evidence.
- This is dispatch-only PM4 command-buffer support. General mixed
command buffers and transfer-heavy command buffers remain on AQL.
- Direct CPU writes into executable resident PM4 storage are still
rejected as an unvalidated publication mode. The default publication
mode is host-copy; async-copy modes remain explicit tuning options.

commit_message:
[Codegen] Skip swizzle transpose when permutation is a no-op modulo unit dims.

The set_encoding pack lowering (and symmetrically the unset_encoding
unpack) currently always emits

  linalg.pack → tensor.expand_shape → linalg.transpose

to apply the swizzle's `permutation` to the packed inner tile. For
many swizzles the permutation only reorders unit dims relative to
non-unit dims (e.g. the generic-scalar 1×1×1 MMA ACC swizzle has
`expandShape = [[CrossIntrinsic(M), Internal(1)], [CrossIntrinsic(N),
Internal(1)]]` with `permutation = [0, 2, 1, 3]` — swapping the
`Internal(1)` placeholders past the `CrossIntrinsic` non-unit dims).
The linearized memory layout of the unpermuted and permuted shapes
is identical there, so the `linalg.transpose` is a no-op in terms of
data movement.

Add `isSwizzlePermutationLayoutNoOp`, a predicate that detects this
case (the permutation, restricted to non-unit source dims, is
order-preserving), and `getSwizzleFoldedReassociation`, which — given
that predicate holds — builds the reassociation that drops the
`linalg.transpose`: the `tensor.expand_shape` (pack side) /
`tensor.collapse_shape` (unpack side) is instead given a
reassociation that lands directly on the permuted shape, partitioning
the permuted inner dims into contiguous slices matching the pack's
`innerTileSizes` one-to-one. Fall through to the existing expand +
transpose lowering when the permutation actually reorders non-unit
dims — the gfx950 scaled-matmul case for instance, where the
permutation moves a size-16 dim past two size-4 dims, must keep the
transpose.

The folded reshape still carries the swizzle's unit dims: the
permuted inner shape is the materialized encoding type fixed by
`getEncodingInfo`, which dialect conversion requires the replacement
value to match exactly — dropping unit dims is not a local choice
here. Hence `getSwizzleFoldedReassociation` only picks a reassociation
reaching that already-fixed shape; whether the materialized type
should carry unit dims at all is a separate, cross-cutting question.

This was motivated by a separate bug in
`hoistOneStaticallyBoundAllocation` (#24483): under dynamic shapes
the intermediate `tensor.empty` between the pack and the transpose
bufferizes to a stack alloca whose size comes from
`ValueBoundsConstraintSet::computeConstantBound` on the dynamic dim,
which for a workload-ordinal dim with only the default `index` umax
constraint (2^53 - 1) produces a ~2^52-element static alloca,
overflows i64 stride math, and lowers to `llvm.alloca poison`.
Eliminating the intermediate via this fast path sidesteps the bug
for the cases that hit this path; the hoist bug is real and the
fix here is in addition to fixing it at the source.

Progress towards #24323.

commit_message:
[Codegen][CPU] Run HoistInnerTiledAccReshapes before vector lowering.

Mirrors the GPU pipeline (`buildLLVMGPUCodegenPassPipeline` adds this
pass right before `UnrollToIntrinsicsPass`). Before this change, on
CPU the reshape ops left around `iree_codegen.inner_tiled` sat
between the K-reduction loop's `scf.for` iter args and the op's
accumulator operand, so the per-tile `HoistableConversionOp` pairs
that the inner_tiled lowering wraps around its ACC
distribute/reassemble couldn't satisfy
`HoistConversionFromLoopPattern`'s strict iter-arg match. They
failed to hoist, got inlined in place, and
`EliminateHoistableConversions` fired a `hoistable_conversion was
not hoisted or cancelled; inlining in place` remark on every CPU
matmul build using the inner_tiled path.

Running `HoistInnerTiledAccReshapes` before
`LLVMCPUVirtualVectorLoweringPass` wraps the prefix/suffix reshape
ops (transpose, shape_cast, broadcast) around the inner_tiled as
`acc_reshape_to_intrinsic` / `acc_reshape_from_intrinsic` hoistable
conversions and runs the elimination over them. The reshapes hoist
out of the K loop, the inner_tiled's accumulator is fed directly by
the iter arg, and the per-tile conversion pairs emitted later in
the vector lowering see direct iter-arg inputs and hoist cleanly.

Progress towards #24323.

commit_message:
[Codegen][CPU] Drop the power-of-two cap on `chooseUnrolling`.

`chooseUnrolling` previously enumerated `intrinsics_m` / `intrinsics_n`
through powers of two. There's no real reason for that — within the
register budget, the cost model can pick any factor.

Looking ahead: some intrinsics may eventually want the unroll factor
on a particular dim to be a multiple of some target-specific number —
Arm scalar-by-element FMA forms are an example, where the scalar is
a lane of a vector register, so covering whole vector registers is
more efficient. But even there it's not a strict preference: narrow
matmuls (e.g. matrix-vector) are better off avoiding the padding
that imposing that multiple would force. So a simple per-intrinsic
"preferred multiple" doesn't capture it. We'll come back to this when
we have a concrete need.

Lit-test fallout: relaxing pow2 lets the cost model land on better
non-pow2 unrolls in some cases the existing tests pin (e.g.
`materialize_encoding_x86_64.mlir`'s dynamic-N AVX-512 case now picks
`intrinsics_m = 29` instead of 16 — saturating the zmm register file
much more tightly, and at higher arithmetic intensity per the
existing scoring formula). CHECK lines updated to the new values.

Progress towards #24323.

commit_message:
[Codegen][CPU] Fix lowerGenericScalarToVectorContract for rank-N inner tiles. (#24488)

After #24455 attaches the per-operand swizzle to the encoder info, the
`inner_tiled` op for the generic-scalar 1×1×1 MMA family receives
operands whose non-unit dim (size = `intrinsics_{m,n,k}`) can sit at any
position in the rank-N tile, not just at the start. The previous
`dropTrailingUnitDims` reduction relied on non-unit dims being leading,
so e.g. an LHS tile of shape `vector<1x1x4x1x1xf32>` (intrinsics_m=4
with N=K=1) collapsed to rank-3 `vector<1x1x4>` instead of the rank-2
`(M, K)` shape `vector.contract` needs — and the wrapper code then
emitted a malformed `vector.broadcast` of `vector<4x1>` into
`vector<1x1x4x1x1>` to glue the result back to the inner_tiled's output
tile.

Switch to a `vector.shape_cast` directly to the canonical `(M, K) / (N,
K) / (M, N)` rank-2 shape: by construction (1×1×1 base intrinsic) every
non-unit dim contributing to an operand tile came from an `intrinsics_*`
cross-intrinsic factor, so the total element count of each operand is
exactly `intrinsics_m * intrinsics_k` (etc.) and the shape_cast is
element-preserving. `shape_cast` the contract result back to the
inner_tiled op's original ACC tile shape so verification matches
downstream.

Progress towards #24323.

[IO] Track async mode on wrapped file handles

Require callers wrapping platform file primitives to declare the file mode properties they are providing. Handles opened or wrapped with IREE_IO_FILE_MODE_ASYNC can be imported into HAL proactors, while handles without that bit remain synchronous-only.

This makes Windows overlapped-handle requirements explicit: duplicate/import failures for declared async handles now propagate as construction errors instead of falling back through a sync-only file.
